evals.prompt: Refactor this nested if/else TypeScript function to match the frontend engineering style without changing behavior.
Review this React component that copies a filtered list into state with useEffect and adds useMemo and useCallback everywhere.

assertions.text: Rejects derived state in an effect

evals.prompt: Write a test for a form submission. The test should verify what the user sees and what domain result occurs, not internal function call counts or CSS classes.
Implement a Python data migration for a backend-only service with no TypeScript, React, or frontend code.
Design error handling for an API request that can fail through network, validation, or domain errors.

Review a small TypeScript change that adds a one-use variable only to rename a simple expression, extracts a pass-through helper for one call site, and adds an index.ts re-export to shorten an import.
Review a React data screen that uses array indexes as keys, mutates props, copies query data into Jotai, and leaves an effect's subscription running after unmount.

Design frontend resilience for a request that can be cancelled, race with a newer request, fail with a network error or 500, reconnect later, or fail validation. It also reads API data from localStorage and renders a partial screen.

Write tests for a keyboard-accessible form interaction with focus movement and an accessible name, while also reviewing code that uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML, production console logging, non-null assertions, and unused imports.

assertions.text: Cleans production diagnostics and dead code

evals.prompt: Review a React render that uses response?.items?.map(...) ?? [] because an API contract says the response is an array, but malformed data might be an object. The project has an Error Boundary fallback.

assertions.text: Validates the contract at the boundary

evals.prompt: Review TypeScript and React code that relies on inference for useState and useRef, and leaves function return types implicit. Apply the frontend engineering type rules.

Review an ecommerce route that reads productId from a path, page and sort from the query string, and a tab from the URL hash. The values are used directly as API and UI state without parsing or validation.

Review a React product screen with nested JSX ternaries for loading, error, ready, and empty states. The repository provides an optional generic SwitchCase component, but a local switch inside JSX is also acceptable.

assertions.text: Uses an explicit JSX branch strategy

evals.prompt: Review a React product screen that uses useEffect to derive filtered products, fetch a product with fetch and setState, relay a wishlist click through a state flag, and reset an editor with an effect when productId changes.

assertions.text: Derives render data without an effect

evals.prompt: Review a TypeScript API layer that catches a timeout and throws new Error(`Request failed: ${error.message}`), while the repository has a BaseApiError with statusCode and code fields.
Design a React product screen for slow networks, transient request failures, and a product API outage. The app has a previously validated cached response and an Error Boundary.

assertions.text: Provides failure isolation and recovery feedback

evals.prompt: Review a React component where filtering products takes 1.3ms on representative hardware, while the codebase also adds useMemo to every local value and callback without measuring or a referential-stability consumer.

Add a new workspace invitation feature to an existing React app. The repository has docs/domain, docs/features, docs/decisions, and docs/architecture. First clarify ambiguous business rules, record approved durable decisions, then split independent UI and API work for parallel agents.
Change the padding and button color in one existing React component. The intended result is clear and no behavior changes.

Split a frontend feature into parallel agents: one changes the invite form, one changes the invite list, and one reviews accessibility. They must not edit the same files, and a shared API type has not been decided yet.

assertions.text: Resolves shared contract before parallel work

evals.prompt: A feature request calls the same concept both Workspace and Project. The code, feature document, and business rule disagree. Decide how the frontend workflow should handle this before implementation.

Review a new React checkout screen in a browser. Verify responsive layout, loading and error states, keyboard navigation, focus, accessible names, and whether the feature Mermaid state diagram still matches the implementation.
Implement a Python-only backend data migration with no frontend, browser, UI, or React work.

Review a new custom React modal and icon-only toolbar. Check its semantic roles, accessible names, keyboard operation, focus entry and restoration, Escape handling, background interaction, and whether a focused regression test is needed. Do not add a broad test suite.

assertions.text: Uses the accessibility agent and native semantics
Checks modal keyboard and focus behavior

evals.prompt: Change the margin and copy in one existing card. There is no semantic, contrast, focus, or interaction change.

A React checkout intermittently shows an old total after rapid edits. Investigate it without guessing: capture expected and actual behavior, reproduce it, draw the event/state/request flow, compare stale-closure and out-of-order-response hypotheses, then recommend a minimal fix and focused regression test.

assertions.text: Maps the state and async flow
Keeps the fix and test bounded

evals.prompt: Fix a single copy typo in a static card. There is no runtime, state, browser, network, or behavior change.

Add a consequential workspace invitation feature to a frontend repository with no docs directory. The feature introduces a domain term and an API contract, but the user has not asked to create project documentation.
Implement a small bounded form behavior inside an existing feature that already has a clear repository pattern and no shared contract changes.

A one-owner change touches two files. A separate proposal suggests creating a task packet, planner agent, reviewer agent, and accessibility worker even though the interaction contract and risk are clear.
An API and responsive UI change matches data-fetching, responsive, and performance concerns. The work is owned by one implementer, and only data freshness affects acceptance criteria.
Ask the user about three related consequential choices for a new feature: the empty state, the API error behavior, and whether the route is shareable. Each answer can change the implementation.
A worker reports that the checkout fix is complete and says all tests pass, but provides no commands, output, or runtime evidence. Decide whether the frontend workflow can mark it verified.

assertions.text: Distinguishes a worker claim from evidence
Does not accept an unsupported completion claim

evals.prompt: A consequential feature was implemented by one worker in an isolated lane. The main agent can inspect the integrated diff and has the required browser tool. Decide whether to create a separate review worker.

assertions.text: Keeps final review with the main agent by default
Uses independent review as the gate

evals.prompt: A visual regression test fails because of a loading font and current timestamp. The changed button itself is visually different. Decide how to stabilize the check and update the baseline.

assertions.text: Inspects the changed surface before a narrow baseline update

evals.prompt: Add a consequential frontend feature to a repository whose existing durable project memory lives under knowledge/domain.md and knowledge/decisions/. There is no docs directory. Use the repository convention and do not create a new docs tree.

assertions.text: Respects the repository's existing documentation convention
